subject: Post-call capacity check & concurrency qualification
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@dataslate.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.g@cloudfin.io>
Date: 2028-03-01T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: performance targets & concurrency for pilot

Hi Hannah / Ben —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can finalize the scope for the pilot: 

Summary of targets we discussed:
- Latency: p95 <= 180 ms for single-turn text generation (average prompt ~120 tokens)
- Sustained throughput: ~300 req/s during business hours (PST)
- Peak burst: up to 1,200 req/s for short windows (5–15 minutes)
- Parallel requests/concurrency: roughly 120 concurrent parallel requests from our service (we multiplex customer sessions over a small set of backend processes)
- Streaming: we rely on partial token streaming to the client; expect ~90 concurrent streaming sessions at peak

Clarifying questions:
1) What are Redwood hosted API default rate limits (per-key and per-connection) and how do they map to these concurrent-session numbers?
2) Do we need Redwood Dedicated to meet these SLOs, or can the hosted tier be configured / quota-increased for a pilot?
3) Any recommended connection-pool or keep-alive settings on our side to maximize utilization and avoid head-of-line issues?

Can you send a succinct proposal with the recommended minimum concurrency/connection settings and any temporary quota increases you can provide for a 6-week pilot? Also please include any documentation we should share with our infra team.

Thanks — happy to sync again if helpful.

Elena Park
Head of Platform
Dataslate AI
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@dataslate.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets & concurrency for pilot

Elena — great summary, thanks. Appreciate the detailed numbers; that helps a lot. High-level answers and an initial proposal below. I copied Ben and Vivek for the technical sizing and to follow the deep-dive.

Quick answers:
- Hosted defaults: our standard public API keys are conservative by design. Typical default limits are in the low hundreds of req/s; they can be increased for pilots but Dedicated/reserved capacity is the most predictable path for sustained p95 targets at ~180ms.
- For your targets (300 sustained, 1,200 peak, 120 concurrent + 90 streaming), we recommend a Dedicated pilot with a small reserved pool plus a burst capacity overlay.

Initial capacity proposal (pilot):
- Reserved concurrency: 200 concurrent request slots (sustained)
- Burst overlay: additional 1,000 concurrent slots usable in short windows for up to 6 hours/day
- Streaming concurrency treated separately: reserve 100 concurrent streaming channels (keeps streaming latency predictable)

What we need from you to firm this up:
- A short sample distribution (requests per second by hour-of-day, average tokens per request, typical request size)
- Any strict SLA requirements (error budget, outage tolerance) and compliance items (SOC2/retention)

I attached a one-page Draft MAP for the pilot and a link to our standard ratecard. Ben / Vivek — please add technical recommendations below (connection pooling, keep-alive, multiplexing).

Next steps:
- Technical deep-dive (30–45m) with Vivek and Ben — suggested windows below
- We’ll produce a pilot PO + temporary quota increase proposal once we get the sample distribution

Thanks,

Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@dataslate.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets & concurrency for pilot

Elena / team — adding some concrete networking and runtime recommendations so you can align infra changes before the deep-dive.

Connection-pool & client-side recommendations:
- Use HTTP/2 with multiplexing where possible; if using HTTP/1.1, maintain persistent keep-alive and aim for ~60s TTL for sockets.
- Target 60–100 persistent connections across your backend fleet for the steady 300 req/s profile; increase to 300 persistent connections when you expect sustained bursts.
- Client parallelism: 6–10 parallel requests per connection is a sweet spot for us in production (reduces head-of-line blocking).

Server/runtime notes (how we interpret your numbers):
- 120 concurrent parallel requests + 90 streaming sessions maps to roughly 210 active token-generation contexts. Accounting for KV cache reuse and batching, we’d size the Dedicated pilot to handle ~250–300 active contexts.
- If you want strict p95 <=180ms across bursts, we recommend enabling per-customer admission control and a small prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts.

Temporary quota proposal for pilot (negotiable):
- Increase hosted quota to allow up to 1,200 concurrent requests for burst windows (5–15m) for the pilot period.
- If you sign a 3-month reserved capacity agreement (Dedicated), we can commit to: 300 sustained concurrent request slots + burst overlay to 3,000 concurrent for a limited time window (we'd need a PO/commit).

Attachments: connpool-proposal.png — shows recommended topology (client pool -> connection multiplexers -> Dedicated frontends).

I’ll cover admission-control knobs and per-route SLOs during the deep-dive.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Samir Gupta <samir.g@cloudfin.io>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets & concurrency for pilot

Thanks — useful detail. Two procurement/ops questions before we lock a PO: 
1) Pricing impact: what is the incremental cost for the Dedicated pilot (300 sustained + burst overlay) vs a temporary hosted quota increase? Please send a conservative estimate / ratecard for both.
2) Compliance/logs: we need 90-day request logs (token redaction applied) and SOC2 evidence for DS. Who owns log retention and how is it exported?

Also looping in our procurement lead (cc’d in my system) — we’ll share a PO template as soon as we have the pricing summary.

Samir
Head of Ops, CloudFin (advising Dataslate)

Samir — good questions. Short answers and proposed next steps below.

Pricing/estimate:
- Temporary hosted quota increase: conservative estimate $12k–$18k / month for the burst windows you described (ephemeral, higher per-unit cost).
- Dedicated pilot (reserved capacity): estimated $28k–$40k / month depending on GPU selection and region; includes admission-control, reserved streaming channels, and higher log retention options.

Compliance/logs:
- Redwood manages request logs; we offer a managed export to your S3 or a secure log-retention bucket. Token-level redaction can be applied server-side before export. 90-day retention is supported as an add-on for pilots. SOC2 artifacts available via our compliance portal — we can provide the evidence package during procurement.

Attachments: Draft_MAP_Dataslate.pdf (pilot milestones, responsibilities, timeline).

Action items / timeline:
- Elena: send sample traffic distribution + PO template (by EOD Fri)
- Redwood (Ben / Vivek): deep-dive to finalize connection sizing and admission-control rules (30–45m)
- Redwood (Hannah): draft pilot agreement and pilot-level ratecard (2 business days after deep-dive)

Proposed deep-dive times (PST):
- Tue 3/6 09:00–09:45
- Wed 3/7 11:00–11:45
- Thu 3/8 15:00–15:45

Please pick one and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,

Hannah
